exposure: Twin type (first twin VD vs. second twin CD)
outcome: Apgar score less than 7 at 5 minutes
cohort: 184 twin pairs where the first twin was born vaginally and the second twin was born via cesarean delivery at Soroka University Medical Center in Israel between 1991 and 2020
finding: There was no significant difference in the long-term incidence of respiratory diseases between twins born vaginally and twins born via cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: While the second twin delivered via cesarean delivery had slightly worse immediate outcomes (non-reassuring fetal heart rate pattern and lower Apgar scores), there was no difference in long-term respiratory diseases compared to the first twin delivered vaginally.
